name: kimi-git-flow
description: Branch-per-task workflow: create a branch, open a PR, wait for CI to be green, merge, and switch back to the default branch. One branch per phase, task, or general code change. Drives `gh` and `git` directly via Bash; no MCP server.
skillInstructions: When the user asks for a code change in a git repo, follow the kimi-git-flow procedure: create a branch named `kimi/<slug>` from the default branch, commit on it, push, open a PR with `gh pr create --fill`, wait for required checks with `gh pr checks --watch`, then `gh pr merge --squash` once green (the remote branch is kept by default; pass `--delete-branch` only when `KIMI_GIT_FLOW_DELETE_REMOTE_BRANCH=1`), and switch the working copy back to the default branch. One branch per phase / task / standalone change. Never force-push the default branch; never merge a red PR; never skip branch-protection rules.

interface.shortDescription: Branch → PR → wait for green → merge, one branch per task.
interface.longDescription: Drives the standard branch-and-PR workflow against GitHub using `gh` and `git`. Creates a branch per phase, task, or general code change; opens a PR; waits for required CI checks; merges when green and returns to the default branch. Exposes slash commands (/branch, /pr, /watch, /merge, /status, /back-to-main) for fine-grained control. GitHub-only; uses `gh` for everything.
